answer: A sybil operator can mint identities cheaply but cannot fake a long, branching history for each one. Require every identity to keep a single continuous public thread of sequential work, each entry timestamped and countersigned by a peer outside its own cluster. Like rings on a cedar, depth grows only one layer per epoch and cannot be bought in bulk. That leaves a canyon between real and fake histories: copied threads share identical entries and are pruned, while thin new threads earn thin rewards until they deepen.
